  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

## Objective
- Finish the existing “BARE METAL” Three.js rustbelt survival game into a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Modify the game directly without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- If doing visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing project and its established game concept.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected core game, UI, world, input, and startup files.
- Installed dependencies successfully with `npm ci`; no vulnerabilities were reported.

### Active
- Identify unfinished gameplay or issues, complete the game, and verify it is playable.

### Blocked
- Build and browser verification have not yet been run after installing dependencies.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining gameplay and startup code to identify unfinished systems or bugs.
2. Implement and build the game.
3. Verify gameplay in a browser; if taking a visual screenshot, follow the JPEG size and latest-only inspection requirements.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js renderer, startup, and main loop.
- `src/game.js`: Game state and survival/job systems.
- `src/world.js`: World and environment construction.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD and interaction UI.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard and touch input.
- `package.json`: Dependencies and build scripts.
- `index.html`: Game page and UI structure.

## Important Context
- `npm ci` completed successfully; prior `npm run build` failed because Vite was not installed at the time (`sh: 1: vite: not found`).
- Git status was clean before dependency installation; no source changes have been made in the recorded work.

## Objective
- Complete the existing “BARE METAL” Three.js rustbelt survival game into a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Modify the game directly without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- If doing visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing project and its established game concept.

## Work State
### Completed
- Installed dependencies with `npm ci`; no vulnerabilities were reported.
- Ran `npm run build` successfully; Vite 7.3.7 built the production output.

### Active
- Identify unfinished gameplay or issues, complete the game, and verify it is playable in a browser.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not yet been run.

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining gameplay and startup code for unfinished systems or bugs.
2. Implement improvements and rebuild.
3. Verify gameplay in a browser; if taking a visual screenshot, follow the JPEG size and latest-only inspection requirements.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js renderer, startup, and main loop.
- `src/game.js`: Game state and survival/job systems.
- `src/world.js`: World and environment construction.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD and interaction UI.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard and touch input.
- `package.json`: Dependencies and build scripts.
- `index.html`: Game page and UI structure.

## Important Context
- `npm run build` completed successfully, transforming 13 modules.
- No source changes have been made; git status was clean before dependency installation.
- `playwright-cli` and `/usr/bin/chromium` are available for browser verification.

655:   buildTrees() {
656:     const rand = mulberry(9182)
657:     const spots = []
658:     for (let i = 0; i < 190; i++) {
659:       let x, z
660:       if (i < 120) {
661:         x = -160 + rand() * 320
662:         z = 34 + rand() * 130
663:       } else {
664:         x = -170 + rand() * 340
665:         z = -140 + rand() * 150
666:       }
667:       if (Math.abs(x) < 18 && z > -15 && z < 38) continue
668:       if (Math.abs(z - 26) < 8) continue
669:       if (Math.hypot(x - 64, z - 42) < 22) continue
670:       if (Math.hypot(x + 58, z - 42) < 20) continue
671:       const scale = 0.7 + rand() * 0.9
672:       spots.push({ x, z, s: scale, pine: rand() > 0.62, rot: rand() * TAU })
673:       this.treeColliders.push({ x, z, r: 0.65 * scale })
674:     }
675:     const trunkGeo = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.13, 0.28, 3.4, 6)
676:     const trunkMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x3f3325, roughness: 1 })
677:     const trunks = new THREE.InstancedMesh(trunkGeo, trunkMat, spots.length)
678:     const pineGeo = new THREE.ConeGeometry(1.7, 4.8, 7)
679:     const leafGeo = new THREE.IcosahedronGeometry(2.0, 1)
680:     const leafMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x56522f, roughness: 1, flatShading: true })
681:     const pineMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x39452f, roughness: 1, flatShading: true })
682:     const pines = new THREE.InstancedMesh(pineGeo, pineMat, spots.filter(s => s.pine).length)
683:     const leaves = new THREE.InstancedMesh(leafGeo, leafMat, spots.filter(s => !s.pine).length)
684:     const m = new THREE.Matrix4()
685:     let qi = 0, li = 0
686:     spots.forEach((s, i) => {
687:       m.compose(V3(s.x, 1.7 * s.s, s.z), new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(0, s.rot, 0)), V3(s.s, s.s, s.s))
688:       trunks.setMatrixAt(i, m)
689:       if (s.pine) {
690:         m.compose(V3(s.x, 3.3 * s.s, s.z), new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(0, s.rot, 0)), V3(s.s, s.s, s.s))
691:         pines.setMatrixAt(qi++, m)
692:       } else {
693:         m.compose(V3(s.x, 3.7 * s.s, s.z), new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(0, s.rot, 0)), V3(s.s * 1.1, s.s * 0.9, s.s * 1.1))
694:         leaves.setMatrixAt(li++, m)
695:       }
696:     })
697:     trunks.castShadow = true; pines.castShadow = true; leaves.castShadow = true
698:     trunks.receiveShadow = true; pines.receiveShadow = true; leaves.receiveShadow = true
699:     this.scene.add(trunks, pines, leaves)

335:   makeBolts(partName, states) {
336:     const info = PART_INFO[partName]
337:     const existing = this.boltMeshes[partName] || []
338:     existing.forEach(b => b.parent?.remove(b))
339:     const list = []
340:     const geo = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.035, 0.035, 0.035, 6)
341:     const positions = []
342:     if (partName === 'wheels') {
343:       // lugs live on each wheel
344:       this.wheels.forEach((wg, wi) => {
345:         for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
346:           const a = i / 4 * Math.PI * 2 + 0.4
347:           positions.push({ x: wg.position.x + Math.cos(a) * 0.2, y: 0.43 + Math.sin(a) * 0.2, z: wg.position.z, parent: this.group })
348:         }
349:       })
350:     } else {
351:       const s = info.spot
352:       const n = info.bolts
353:       for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
354:         positions.push({ x: s.x + (i - (n - 1) / 2) * 0.16, y: s.y + 0.14, z: s.z + 0.08, parent: this.group })
355:       }
356:     }
357:     positions.forEach((p, i) => {
358:       const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, states?.[i] === 'loose' ? this.boltMaterialLoose : states?.[i] === 'stripped' ? this.boltMaterialStrip : this.boltMaterialGood)
359:       if (partName === 'wheels') {
360:         m.position.set(p.x, p.y, p.z)
361:         m.rotation.z = Math.PI / 2
362:       } else {
363:         m.position.set(p.x, p.y, p.z)
364:       }
365:       m.visible = this.installed[partName] !== false
366:       this.group.add(m)
367:       list.push(m)
368:     })
369:     this.boltMeshes[partName] = list
370:     return list
371:   }

373:   update(dt, speed = 0) {
374:     this.spin += speed * dt * 2.3
375:     this.wheels.forEach(w => {
376:       if (w.visible) w.children.forEach(c => { c.rotation.y = this.spin })
377:     })
378:     if (this.engineRunning) {
379:       const feel = Math.min(1, Math.abs(speed) / 8)
380:       this.group.position.y = Math.sin(performance.now() * 0.05) * 0.0025 * (1 + feel * 4)
381:       this.group.rotation.z = Math.sin(performance.now() * 0.031) * 0.0008 * (1 + feel * 5)
382:     } else {
383:       this.group.rotation.z *= 0.98
384:     }
385:   }
386: }

## Objective
- Complete the existing “BARE METAL” Three.js rustbelt survival game into a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Modify the game directly without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- If doing visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing project and its established game concept.

### Completed
- Installed dependencies with `npm ci`; no vulnerabilities were reported.
- Ran `npm run build` successfully.
- Inspected core game, UI, input, and world code; searched for TODO/FIXME and placeholder markers.

### Active
- Identify unfinished gameplay or issues, implement improvements, and verify the game is playable in a browser.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not yet been run.

1. Inspect remaining gameplay and startup code for unfinished systems or bugs.
2. Implement improvements and rebuild.
3. Verify gameplay in a browser; follow screenshot requirements if taking a visual screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results.

- `src/main.js`: Three.js renderer, startup, and main loop.
- `src/game.js`: Game state and survival/job systems.
- `src/world.js`: World and environment construction.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD and interaction UI.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard and touch input.
- `src/truck.js`: Vehicle and repair-part definitions.
- `index.html`: Game page and UI structure.
- `package.json`: Dependencies and build scripts.

- `npm run build` completed successfully with Vite 7.3.7, transforming 13 modules.

- Git status was clean before dependency installation; no source changes have been made.
- `playwright-cli` and `/usr/bin/chromium` are available for browser verification.
